title: Plugin Developer Listing and Review Terms

p.text: This is a pre-release draft. Items marked 【TBD】 or ［　］ will be decided before the official version is published.
p.detail: rasq.developer / version 1.0.0-draft.20261007. Reference translation of the user-facing text of the Japanese draft (tool/legal/build_legal.py).

p.text: Reference translation. This is a reference translation provided for convenience. The Japanese version is the official text, and if there is any difference between them, the Japanese version governs.

source.text: 1. The developer shall accurately submit their name or corporate name, contact details, the products in which they hold rights, and the necessary tax and settlement information. If any of these change, the developer shall update them. The Operator may request supporting documents to the extent necessary.

2. The developer name and support contact for each Plugin are displayed in the Store. Except for items required to be displayed by law, personal information submitted for review and non-public contact details are not made public.

3. The Operator is responsible for sales to users, collection of payments, purchase history, and acceptance of refunds, and the developer is responsible for development, accurate descriptions, maintenance, rights clearance, and responding to technical inquiries. Products for which no sales and settlement conditions have been agreed are not sold for a fee.

1. The developer shall submit parts that the developer created or for which the developer has obtained a lawful license, and shall clearly state the license, copyright notices, notices required for distribution, source disclosure obligations, and terms of use for materials, fonts, models, and the like. The developer must not warrant that it holds third-party rights without confirming the rights holder's permission.

2. The developer grants the Operator a non-exclusive right to reproduce, transmit to the public, and convert the format of the submission and promotional materials to the extent necessary for review, storage, distribution, re-provision to users who have purchased it, safety measures, and presentation in the Store. This does not automatically permit modification of the content or its diversion to other products.

3. Source code submitted for review is not included in distributions to general users. Viewers are limited to Operator staff who need it for review and safety responses and to processing contractors managed under contract. If an external AI review service is used, the recipient, country or region, scope of what is sent, retention period, and whether it is used for training are displayed before submission. These conditions do not include permission to use non-public source code to train AI models or to develop other products.

4. Even after the agreement ends, the license survives to the extent necessary for rights already acquired by users, proof of purchase history, handling of refunds and disputes, and retention required by law. New sales and distribution end. The specific retention periods and deletion methods are set out in Article 7.

5. The licenses for the SDK, samples, Plugins, and materials are each displayed separately. Where redistribution is prohibited, the proprietary files and materials subject to the prohibition, the exceptions, the backups users may make, and the like are specified. Rights to modify and redistribute granted by third-party licenses are not prohibited.

p.title: Article 3. Submitted Information and Safety Conditions

source.text: 1. For each version, the developer shall submit the distribution, version, changes, permissions and the reasons for them, communication destinations, data handled, retention period, deletion method, support contact, and license. If source code or build procedures are requested for review, the developer shall submit verifiable materials with confidential information removed.

2. The developer must not engage in unnecessary acquisition of authentication information or user data, undeclared external transmission, use of permissions before consent, unauthorized disclosure of limited-visibility data, disguising of billing or publishing operations, evasion of review, or violation of the licenses of dependent libraries.

3. If communication destinations or data handled are expanded, the developer shall declare it as a change even if the permission names are the same, and shall have the new version reviewed. Listed binaries or the content of the same version may not be replaced without review.

4. The developer shall manage the developer key, and if a leak or unauthorized use is suspected, shall immediately contact the Operator to revoke and replace it. A signature does not relieve the developer of responsibility for the accuracy of review information or for safety.
5. If a vulnerability, rights infringement, or data incident is discovered, the developer shall promptly inform
［TBD: security contact］
of the affected versions, the impact, and planned measures, and shall cooperate in containing the damage, notifying users, and distributing a fixed version.

1. Review combines deterministic checks, automated and AI-based evaluation, and confirmation by a person. Approval may be given through automated processing, but a final refusal to list is not confirmed solely because an automated evaluation was inconclusive or negative; a person reviews it again.

2. For approval, return for revision, holding, or suspension, the Operator notifies the developer of the version concerned, the main reasons, and whether corrections or additional materials are required. Information that would directly lead to the spread of harm or the evasion of checks, and information about reporters and third parties, may be withheld to the extent necessary for protection.
3. The developer may appeal by submitting grounds and materials to
［TBD: contact for developer review inquiries and re-review］
. A person at the Operator reconsiders the matter and notifies the developer of the result. Requests to lift account sanctions and appeals against product reviews are accepted separately.

4. Passing review does not guarantee continued listing in the future, operation in all environments, or non-infringement of third-party rights. Even after review, the Operator may investigate discrepancies between declarations and behavior.

1. When applying for review for listing or of a new version, the developer pays the review fee displayed on the application screen. The amount of the review fee is determined by the formula displayed on the application screen, based on the number of pieces obtained by counting the content of the files included in the distribution of the version applied for, using the measurement method published by the Operator (including the vocabulary used for measurement and its version). The byte size of the distribution is only a guide, and the amount may differ depending on the content even for the same size. The developer can confirm the same number of pieces and amount before applying by using the measurement tool provided by the Operator. Before the application, the following are displayed: the amount (including tax) and a breakdown of its calculation (number of pieces, measurement method, and formula); the version and scope covered; the checks included in the review (automated checks, AI-based evaluation, confirmation by a person, and the number of re-reviews after return for revision); estimated times for starting and for notification of the result; payment methods; and the conditions for cancellation and refunds. Payment is made through Stripe, and the application is formed when payment is completed and receipt of the application is notified.

2. The review fee is a fee for the work of reviewing. It does not guarantee approval, continued listing, display order in the Store, number of users, or sales. No refund is given solely because the result of the review is return for revision or non-approval.

3. In the following cases, the full review fee is refunded: (1) the developer cancels the application before the review is started; (2) the Operator decides not to accept the review; (3) the Operator has not started the review by the estimated start time in Section 7 after receipt of the application, and the developer cancels the application; (4) the Operator has not notified the result (approval, return for revision, or non-approval) by the estimated result notification time in Section 7 after starting the review, and the developer cancels the application before the result is notified; (5) a double payment, an erroneous charge, or another payment error; (6) upon reconsideration of an appeal, it is confirmed that non-approval or return for revision was due to the Operator's error.
4. If an application for which the review fee was paid is returned for revision, and the developer, within
【TBD: 30 days】

of the notice of return for revision, submits a version of the same Plugin as a correction for that return for revision, specifying the returned application, it is re-reviewed without an additional review fee, for the first time only. If an application re-reviewed without an additional review fee is returned for revision again, this treatment does not apply. Submissions that do not specify the returned application, submissions after the deadline, regular updates, and submissions of other Plugins are treated as new applications and incur a review fee.
5. No fee is charged for an appeal under Article 4, Section 3. Whether or not a review fee was paid does not change the review criteria, the result, or the level of detail of the reasons notified.

6. For the time being, the Operator conducts reviews with a small team. When applications are concentrated or in similar situations, the Operator may be unable to start or notify the result by the estimated times in Section 7. When this is expected, the Operator will inform the applicant, before the estimated date, of the expected delay and the new expected date. This notice does not change the estimated times in Section 7 or the refund conditions in Section 3.

7. In this article, "start" means that the Operator has begun the review of that version (by running automated checks and the reviewer recording the start), and the Operator notifies the applicant when it starts. The estimated start time is within
【TBD: 30 days】
of receipt of the application, and the estimated result notification time is within
【TBD: 30 days】
of the start; each date is displayed on the application screen.
8. This article does not restrict any rights the developer has under law.

1. Paid products are sold after the price, tax-inclusive display, scope of updates covered, the Operator's commission, calculation of the settlement amount, tax treatment, settlement date, transfer fees, and minimum settlement amount have been agreed in a separate schedule of sales conditions.

2. Settlement is based on the consideration actually used by users for purchases. When points are purchased, they are not yet confirmed as sales of any particular developer. The method of allocating free points, discounts, and campaign costs is also specified in the separate schedule.

3. Settlement statements show sales by product, refunds, cancellations, payment costs, the agreed commission, tax adjustments, and amounts carried forward. If a reserve is necessary in connection with refunds or unauthorized use, the Operator notifies the grounds, the amount concerned, and when it will be reviewed, and does not withhold unrelated sales indefinitely.

4. Refunds to users and settlement adjustments with developers are made according to the cause and the responsibility of the parties. Payment failures or erroneous charges by the Operator are not automatically passed on in full to the developer. Reasonable refunds due to a developer's false declarations or serious defects may be adjusted under the agreed conditions.
5. The developer may request confirmation of notified settlement details at
［TBD: settlement inquiry contact］
. Even if a short inquiry period is set, it will not be a condition that uniformly waives claims for calculation errors or claims under law.

p.title: Article 6. End of Listing and Liability

source.text: 1. The developer may apply to end new sales. The end date is announced after the handling of re-acquisition, support, refunds, and security updates for existing users has been arranged with the Operator. In emergencies such as rights infringement or serious incidents, distribution may be stopped first.

2. Depending on the nature of the violation or risk, the Operator may issue a warning, suspend a specific version, end the listing, or restrict developer privileges. Where possible, the Operator shows the reasons and an opportunity for correction in advance, and accepts appeals even after an emergency suspension.

3. Use, modification, and redistribution permitted by third-party licenses are not prohibited merely because of the end of the listing or of the agreement. If there are features that can no longer be provided to existing purchasers, the Operator and the developer will respond with fixes, alternatives, or refunds according to the cause.

4. Each party is liable, in accordance with law and individually agreed conditions, for damage it causes to the other party or to users through its own responsibility. There is no indemnity clause that unconditionally places all disputes and third-party claims on one party.

1. The Operator handles the developer's application details, contact details, the public key of the developer key, notes for signature recovery, the submitted distributions and source code, review records, and records of review fee payments for the purposes of review, distribution, settlement, safety responses, and responding to inquiries. Matters not provided for in this article are governed by the Privacy Policy.

2. In review, in addition to deterministic checks, the Operator uses an assessment system it manages and an external AI. The submitted distributions and source code are sent to the external AI. The current recipient is OpenAI (Codex, United States). The Operator also uses Alibaba's Qwen model running on the Operator's computers, but processing by this model does not involve sending anything externally. The Operator confirms, through its agreement with the recipient, the condition that the content sent is not used for AI training. If the recipient changes, it is displayed before the application.

3. Source code submitted for review is not distributed to users. While the Plugin is listed, it is retained for re-review and safety responses, and it is deleted one year after the end of the listing.

4. Records of review fee payments are retained for eight years from the end of the fiscal year of the transaction. After the developer's account is deleted, they are retained with the account replaced by an identifier not linked to the account, and with free-text entries such as application notes erased.

5. Records of which version was reviewed when and with what result are retained even after the end of the listing, for user safety and dispute handling. The reviewers' and developer's accounts are disconnected from the records after the account is deleted.

6. Even if the developer's account is deleted, Plugins already listed remain in the Store until the procedures in Article 6 are completed. The developer's display name is replaced with the post-deletion display.
